key: And I will establish My covenant between Me and thee and thy seed after thee throughout their generations for an everlasting covenant, to be a God unto thee and to thy seed after thee.
s: In Genesis 17 God appears to Abram, renames him Abraham and promises him nations and land; Sforno, on Genesis 17:7, reads His promise to be their God as binding His name to them without intermediary, so that, keeping the covenant, they endure for ever.
src: Sforno, Commentary on the Torah, Genesis 17:7, Hebrew (On Your Way), Sefaria export commit 3f10136 (2026)

evidence.words: להיות לך לאלהים ולזרעך אחריך. ליחד שמי עליכם בלתי אמצעי … שבהקמת הברית ושמירתו יהיו הוא וזרעו נצחיי' באיש לפניו
evidence.gloss: ‘To be a God unto thee and to thy seed after thee’: to bind My name upon you without intermediary … that through the establishing of the covenant and its keeping he and his seed would be everlasting, a man ever standing before Him.

reason: Both problems hold. (1) The old reading ‘reads the promise’ followed ‘nations and land’ and so attached to the wrong promise; Sforno’s lemma is להיות לך לאלהים ולזרעך אחריך, the promise to be their God, and ליחד שמי עליכם is ‘to bind My name upon you’, not ‘unite with’. The reading now names that promise without quotation (the critic’s ‘a God unto thee’ is four words of the key, over rule 3’s three) and says ‘binding His name to them’. (2) src now names the Hebrew edition read, ‘On Your Way’, as the packet gives it, matching d014. Re-opened packet.js tanakh 5 --verse 17:7: the lemma and the words are verbatim. verse.js ok (Genesis 17:7, at [16,7]); entry-check ok, no warns. Commentator and reading otherwise unchanged.
